source_refs.note: Topic 18.2.2 with the Performing and Recording box (printed 'Recoding') and the Analyzing problems, answered (PDF 89-90).

blocks.text: Genes pass from one generation to the next at random, so the chance of new allele combinations is worked out with mathematical probability: how often a particular outcome occurs. For one or two genes (such as RrYy x RrYy) a Punnett square works, but for many genes (such as AaBbCcDdEe x AaBbCcDdEe) it becomes too large, and the rules of probability are used instead.

Probability is the number of times an event occurs divided by the total number of possible outcomes. If wrinkled seeds appear 1,850 times out of 7,324 seeds, the probability is 1,850 / 7,324 = 0.253, about 1 seed in 4.
The chance of two or more independent events happening together is the product of their separate probabilities. A six on one dice is 1/6, so two sixes on two dice is 1/6 x 1/6 = 1/36.

items: Aa x Aa: each parent gives an a gamete with probability 1/2, so aa offspring = 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4.
RrYy x RrYy: round = 3/4 and yellow = 3/4, so round yellow = 3/4 x 3/4 = 9/16.

blocks.text: For mutually exclusive events, only one of which can happen at a time, the probability of either is the sum of their separate probabilities. On a six-sided dice, getting 1 or 6 is 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3. In Aa x Aa the dominant phenotype arises in three ways, A + A, A + a and a + A, each with probability 1/4, so its probability is 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

blocks.title: Performing and recording: rolling a dice
blocks.text: Use the rules of probability to calculate the probability of getting sixes when you roll a dice 100 times.
